recentItems.title: Tomorrow's World (Nov 1993) BBC 3D week with Doctor Who: Dimensions In Time preview/making-of
recentItems.description:
Tomorrow's World (Nov 1993) BBC 3D week with Doctor Who: Dimensions In Time preview/making-of

In 1993, the BBC did a week of selected programmes in 3D.  Unlike previous efforts at 3D TV (which were in red-cyan anaglyph) such as ITV's try in the 1980s, this time the Pulfrich effect was used (the two TV interlaced fields - slightly different due to movement - being forced to different brightnesses by light/dark glasses, and consequently interpreted by the brain at different speeds and thus assumed to belong to the same moment in time and thus presented as 3D). See the programme for full info about the technique.

A showcase programme to use the technique was the 30th anniversary two-part "Doctor Who" special called "Dimensions In Time".  The clip here features a making-of segment about the show.

The Pulfrich 3D effect (as with the red-green version) was a pain to the viewer (it required the picture to be constantly moving in a certain direction and at a certain rate) and unsurprisingly didn't take off.   In more recent times, 3D TV once more failed, proving the public were less interested than TV providers thought.

Anyway, unfortunately, the "Who" special wasn't very good.  Additionally, "Tomorrow's World" as seen here is on its last legs IMHO - we've gone from James Burke in the 1960s to Howard Stableford (shudder) here in the 1990s.  How it stumbled on for ten more years is beyond me. 

TECH NOTE

I have uploaded the clip at 50fps even though it's from VHS. This means the effect (should you have the light/dark glasses) should still vaguely work (provided you have selected 720p50 in the cog resolution settings).   I can upload "Dimensions In Time" the same way, if there is enough interest (assuming the BBC doesn't strike it, and assuming it isn't on Youtube already at 50fps).

Dad's Army missing episode appeal by David Croft. BBC 1998.
recentItems.description:
An appeal from Dad's Army producer and writer, David Croft, for finding the missing episodes of Dad's Army (all from the 2nd series, in 1969).

It should be pointed out that in the video recorders shown, at least one (haven't checked the others) couldn't possibly have recorded the missing episodes (which were shown - domestically at least - once in 1969) as the Philips 1500 hadn't been invented for 3 years yet!   I should also point out that Croft says, "Before the video cassette recorder was developed..." and then goes onto show the 1500 which is obviously that very thing!

NB Since this was made, two of the episodes mentioned - "Operation Kilt" and "The Battle of Godfrey's Cottage" - have been found, leaving three missing episodes.  It should be noted, however, that radio versions of these exist. All three have also been remade with animation and the original soundtrack (either the TV soundtrack or the radio episode). All three were also remade with a new cast by UKTV Gold in 2019.
